materials.name: Metals and alloys
materials.imaging: Specular surfaces: use diffuse dome or dark-field lighting; avoid direct glare.

materials.name: Plastics and polymers
materials.imaging: Back-lighting reveals voids in translucent parts; polarizers reduce glare.

materials.name: Wood
materials.imaging: Natural grain varies widely: train anomaly models per species and finish.

materials.name: Glass
materials.imaging: Use back-light or dark-field; front-lit photos mostly show reflections.

materials.name: Ceramics
materials.imaging: Low-angle lighting accentuates surface relief (pores, chips).

materials.name: Textiles and fabrics
materials.imaging: Keep fabric flat and tensioned; periodic weave suits reference/anomaly models.

materials.name: Leather and hides
materials.imaging: Lay the hide flat. Low-angle (raking) light reveals scratches, wrinkles and grain defects; diffuse light reveals stains and colour variation. Natural grain differs per hide and finish: learn the reference from the same article and colour.

materials.name: Rubber
materials.imaging: Black, low-contrast surfaces need strong directional lighting.

materials.name: Paper and cardboard
materials.imaging: Transmitted light exposes thin spots and holes.

materials.name: Composites
materials.imaging: Sub-surface delamination is not visible optically; pair with NDT.

materials.name: Electronic components
materials.imaging: Golden-template comparison needs fixed magnification and registration.

materials.name: Construction materials
materials.imaging: Shoot perpendicular to the surface with a scale reference for crack widths.

materials.name: Other / custom material
materials.imaging: Start with the screening detector, collect good samples, then fit an anomaly model.
